newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr off highs vs yen in Tokyo, mood still bullish.
newsitem.headline: Dlr off highs vs yen in Tokyo, mood still bullish.

text.p: 0620 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar was off its highs against the yen by late afternoon Tokyo on Wednesday, but the market was still bullish towards the greenback after a sharp rise overnight, traders said.
"A lot of people turned into dollar bulls after the dollar jumped above 115 yen overnight. Interbank players were setting up new longs," said a trader at a long-term bank.
The dollar closed at 115.74/79 and 1.7930/40 marks in New York on Tuesday.
Some traders were more cautious about buying dollars ahead of the release of Japan's customs-cleared trade data for June on Thursday and the U.S. international trade data for May on Friday.
"Dollar longs are building up. I fear that dollar/yen may be on a roller-coaster that is approaching the summit," a city bank trader said.
Still, others said any dollar dip after the trade figure release could provide a bargain-hunting oppportunity.
Economists' forecasts for Japan's June trade surplus ranged from 971.0 billion yen to 1.61 trillion yen, or a rise of between 33 percent to 120 percent from a year earlier.
The data will be announced at 8.50 a.m. on Thursday (2350 GMT Wednesday).
"The market already knows that the surplus will expand sharply. Unless there is a big surprise, the impact may be limited," said a trader at a trust bank.
Sporadic selling by Japanese exporters capped the greenback, with more offers expected to emerge above 115.80 yen, traders said.
In addition to exporter sales, earlier hedge-related selling by Japanese investors also helped to cap the dollar's upside, traders said.

The bullish sentiment towards the dollar was also fuelled by widespread market talk that an influential U.S. hedge fund has been buying one-year dollar call options in heavy amounts at around 125 yen over the past several days, traders said.
The dollar drew some bids in early afternoon trade following news that North and South Korean soldiers exchanged fire at the border, but the impact was short-lived, traders said.
The dollar was steady against the mark by late Tokyo.

The greenback slipped versus the mark earlier as players squared dollar/mark longs ahead of a planned statement by the German cabinet calling for a strong mark and a strong euro due later on Wednesday.
The German currency was well-supported versus the yen on short-covering interest, but the upside was heavy near 65 yen, traders said.
The mark stood at around 64.47/50 yen, compared with around 64.55 yen on late Tuesday in New York.
Singapore dealers said the dollar/mark was showing softness after giving up its overnight gains and ending lower in New York on comments by German officials about the dollar having risen too far.

"I'm quite taken aback. After last night, I thought the dollar/mark would come back up and yet it went down all the way. I think people are quite afraid to buy today," a European bank dealer said. He said the dollar/mark should find some support at the 1.7835/40 level, while 1.7950 would be resisted.
-- Singapore newsroom (65-8703080) -- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk 81-3-3432-9780
